source: Quiz 3 - Sessions 1-4: Model Size, Thinking, and Skills
question: By the original working definition described in the lecture, roughly when did the instructor argue the field actually crossed the AGI (artificial general intelligence) threshold?

options.text: At the moment Astra was released, during this class session.
options.feedback: The argument placed the crossing well before this release. Astra came up as the occasion for revisiting the definition, not as the moment the bar was met.

options.text: It has not been crossed yet by any released model.
options.feedback: This is the opposite of the argument made in class, which was that the line had already been passed under the older definition and simply went unremarked.

options.text: Sometime in the era of expert systems, decades ago.
options.feedback: The notes place the crossing far more recently -- about a year and a half before this lecture -- not in an earlier era of AI.

options.text: Roughly 18 months before this lecture, largely unnoticed.
options.feedback: That is the claim made in class, under the older and more modest definition of AGI. It is offered as the instructor's own reading of the timeline rather than a settled finding in the field.
